theory.intro: One linear relationship can appear as a **pattern**, a **table of values**, an **equation**, a **set of coordinates**, and a **straight-line graph**. All five describe the same pairs of $x$- and $y$-values, so you can move between them and check that they agree.
facts: A table column with $x=a$ and $y=b$ is the coordinate $(a,b)$, and the same pair is one point on the graph.
To decide whether two representations match, compare the $y$-values they give at the same $x$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A pattern begins at $10$ when $x=1$ and decreases by $2$ each time $x$ increases by $1$. Complete the table, then choose the matching table.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$

$A=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&8&6&4\end{array}$

$B=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&9&8&7\end{array}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract $2$ for each increase of $1$ in $x$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&8&6&4\end{array}$

Table $A$ has the same starting value and decrease.

workedExamples.question_text:
Use $y=-2x+3$ to complete the table.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$

workedExamples.solution_text:
The marked points are $(0,1)$, $(1,3)$, $(2,5)$ and $(3,7)$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&1&3&5&7\end{array}$

Table $A$ matches every marked point.

Both equations give $y=5$ at $x=0$. Read another marked point: $(1,3)$.

For $y=-2x+5$ at $x=1$:

$\begin{aligned}y&=-2(1)+5\\&=3\end{aligned}$

For $y=-x+5$ at $x=1$:

$\begin{aligned}y&=-(1)+5\\&=4\end{aligned}$

The graph matches $y=-2x+5$. Its other marked points, $(2,1)$ and $(3,-1)$, also agree with this equation.

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the equation represented by the table. Check the column for $x=8$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccccc}x&0&1&2&3&4&8\\\hline y&-4&-1&2&5&8&20\end{array}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
For each increase of $1$ in $x$, $y$ increases by $3$. At $x=0$, $y=-4$.

$y=3x-4$

For $x=8$:

$\begin{aligned}y&=3(8)-4\\&=20\end{aligned}$

This agrees with the table.

Read the marked points to make a table.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&-1&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&4&2&0&-2&-4\end{array}$

For each increase of $1$ in $x$, $y$ decreases by $2$. The graph crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,2)$.

$y=-2x+2$

foundation.question_text:
A pattern begins at $6$ when $x=1$ and increases by $3$ each time $x$ increases by $1$.
Complete the table: $\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&6&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$.

A pattern begins at $3$ when $x=1$ and increases by $4$ each time $x$ increases by $1$.
Which table describes the pattern: $A=\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&1&2&3\\\hline y&3&7&11\end{array}$ or $B=\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&1&2&3\\\hline y&3&6&9\end{array}$?

A pattern begins at $8$ when $x=1$ and decreases by $2$ each time $x$ increases by $1$.
Complete the table: $\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&8&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=5,ymin=-1,ymax=7,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3,4,5},ytick={0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.7:4.3,samples=2] {x+3};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(0,3) (1,4) (2,5) (3,6)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Does the table $\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&3&4&5&6\end{array}$ describe the same relationship as the graph?
foundation.solution_text:
$(0,3),(1,4),(2,5),(3,6)$
Yes; every column is a marked point on the line.

foundation.question_text:
A pattern begins at $4$ when $x=1$ and increases by $3$ each time $x$ increases by $1$.
Which table describes the same pattern: $A=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&4&7&10&13\end{array}$ or $B=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&4&8&12&16\end{array}$?

development.question_text: Use the equation $y=4x-1$ to complete the table: $\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&0&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$.
Use the equation $y=-3x+2$ to complete the table: $\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&0&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=4,ymin=-1,ymax=7,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3,4},ytick={0,2,4,6},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.3:3.4,samples=2] {-2*x+6};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(0,6) (1,4) (2,2) (3,0)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The graph passes through the marked points.
Which equation matches it: $y=-2x+6$ or $y=-x+6$?

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=4,ymin=-1,ymax=10,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3,4},ytick={0,2,4,6,8,10},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.3:3.4,samples=2] {2*x+3};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(0,3) (1,5) (2,7) (3,9)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which table matches the displayed graph: $A=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&3&5&7&9\end{array}$ or $B=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&3&4&5&6\end{array}$?
Find the equation represented by the table: $\begin{array}{c|cccccc}x&0&1&2&3&4&12\\\hline y&-3&1&5&9&13&45\end{array}$.
development.solution_text:
$y$ increases by $4$ each time $x$ increases by $1$, and $y=-3$ when $x=0$.
$y=4x-3$
At $x=12$, $4(12)-3=45$, as shown in the table.

mastery.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-2,xmax=5,ymin=-10,ymax=10,xtick={-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4,5},xticklabels={-2,-1,0,1,{},3,4,5},ytick={-10,-8,-6,-4,-2,0,2,4,6,8,10},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-1.4:4.4,samples=2] {-3*x+4};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(-1,7) (0,4) (1,1) (2,-2) (3,-5) (4,-8)};\node[anchor=north,font=\small,fill=white,inner sep=1pt,yshift=-3pt] at (axis cs:2,0) {$2$};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Find the equation represented by the graph.
mastery.solution_text:
$y=4$ when $x=0$.
The marked points show that $y$ decreases by $3$ each time $x$ increases by $1$.
$y=-3x+4$

mastery.question_text: Find the equation represented by the table: $\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}x&0&1&2&3&4&-6&15\\\hline y&11&6&1&-4&-9&41&-64\end{array}$.
mastery.solution_text:
$y$ decreases by $5$ each time $x$ increases by $1$, and $y=11$ when $x=0$.
$y=-5x+11$
At $x=-6$, $-5(-6)+11=41$; at $x=15$, $-5(15)+11=-64$.
